details: Financial markets are keenly awaiting crucial US inflation data this week, including the Producer Price Index (PPI) on Thursday and the Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Friday. These reports are the final major readings before the Federal Reserve's September 15-16 meeting, where there's a significant probability (around 58-60%) of a 25-basis-point rate hike. Concurrently, the European Central Bank (ECB) is widely anticipated to raise its benchmark rates by 25 basis points on September 10 to curb inflation. These tightening monetary policies generally create headwinds for risk assets like cryptocurrencies, with Bitcoin showing price sensitivity to these developments.
title: Markets Brace for US Inflation Data, Fed & ECB Rate Decisions

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) released a report on September 2, 2026, outlining progress in the digital euro's preparation phase. This report details work on offline functionality, privacy mechanisms, and holding limits. While this update does not constitute final political authorization for issuance, it signifies continued development of Europe's central bank digital currency (CBDC) project, potentially impacting bank liquidity management and influencing future crypto and DeFi policy discussions.
title: ECB Progresses Digital Euro Preparation Phase

details: Speculation about an interest rate hike by the Bank of Japan (BoJ) in September has intensified, with Polymarket data indicating a 98% probability for a 25-basis-point increase. This follows upbeat wage growth data and a revised Q2 GDP figure in Japan, which have strengthened expectations for a BoJ rate increase. Such a move, which would bring benchmark rates to their highest since 1995, could influence global liquidity and affect cryptocurrency markets, particularly concerning yen carry trades.
title: BOJ Rate Hike Bets Intensify Amid Strong Japanese Data

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) highlighted on September 8, 2026, how digital currencies and artificial intelligence (AI) are poised to reshape global payment systems, making them more efficient and scalable. The IMF emphasizes the critical need for secure, auditable, and regulatory-compliant infrastructures to maintain trust in these evolving systems. This broader focus on digital finance infrastructure, including CBDCs and stablecoins, aims to lower costs and foster new business models, representing a long-term strategic view rather than immediate market-moving news.
title: IMF Discusses Digital Currencies and AI Reshaping Payments
